statements: Prophet Nuh built an ark.
Prophet Musa was given the Tawrat.
Prophet Nuh was given the Tawrat.
easy.explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa. No scripture is named in the Qur'an as having been given to Nuh.

statements: Maryam is the mother of Prophet Isa.
Maryam is named in the Qur'an.
Maryam was a prophet.
easy.explain: Maryam is honoured as chosen above the women of the worlds, and a surah bears her name, but she is not counted among the prophets.

statements: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu alaykum.
The greeting means peace be upon you.
The greeting is only used once a year.
easy.explain: The greeting of peace is used in everyday life, whenever Muslims meet.

statements: Fasting is obligatory during Ramadan.
Children before puberty are not obliged to fast.
Everyone without exception must fast, including the seriously ill.
easy.explain: The Qur'an exempts the sick and the traveller, who make up the days later; those permanently unable to fast give fidyah instead.

statements: The Qur'an has 114 surahs.
Surah An-Nas is the last surah.
Surah An-Nas is the first surah.
easy.explain: An-Nas is surah 114, the last. Al-Fatihah is the first.

statements: Hajj takes place in Makkah.
Tawaf is performed around the Ka'bah.
Tawaf is performed around Mount Arafah.
easy.explain: Tawaf is the circling of the Ka'bah. Arafah is a plain where pilgrims stand on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah; there is no circling there.

statements: Angels are created from light, according to hadith.
Angels do not disobey Allah.
Angels are a kind of prophet.
easy.explain: Angels and prophets are entirely distinct. Prophets are human beings chosen from among people.

statements: Muslims believe in all the prophets.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the first prophet.
easy.explain: Adam, ʿalayhi al-salām, is the first. Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet, the seal of the prophets.

statements: Salah is performed five times a day.
Each salah has a set number of rak'ahs.
Each of the five prayers has the same number of rak'ahs.
easy.explain: Fajr has two rak'ahs, Maghrib three, and Dhuhr, Asr and Isha four each.

statements: The Qur'an is the word of Allah.
It was revealed through the angel Jibril.
It was written by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself.
easy.explain: The Qur'an is revelation, not authorship. It was conveyed through Jibril, memorised and recorded by scribes among the companions.

statements: A mosque is a place of worship.
The imam leads the congregational prayer.
The imam must be an angel.
easy.explain: The imam is a person who leads the prayer; any qualified Muslim man may do so.

statements: Zakat helps those in need.
Sadaqah is voluntary.
Sadaqah is obligatory and zakat is voluntary.
easy.explain: It is the other way round: zakat is obligatory with fixed rules, while sadaqah is voluntary.

statements: Laylat al-Qadr falls in Ramadan.
Eid al-Fitr falls in Shawwal.
Laylat al-Qadr falls in Shawwal.
easy.explain: Laylat al-Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan. Shawwal is the month that follows, beginning with Eid al-Fitr.

statements: Prophet Ibrahim is associated with the Ka'bah.
Prophet Isma'il was his son.
Prophet Musa was his son.
easy.explain: Isma'il and Ishaq were sons of Ibrahim. Musa came many generations later.

statements: The adhan is the call to prayer.
It is called before each obligatory prayer.
It is called only on Fridays.
easy.explain: The adhan precedes each of the five daily prayers, every day.

statements: Muslims fast from food and drink while fasting.
The fast is broken at sunset.
The fast is broken at midnight.
easy.explain: The fast ends at sunset with iftar, at the time of the Maghrib prayer.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah opens the Qur'an.
It is recited in every rak'ah.
It has seventy ayahs.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs, not seventy.

statements: Jibril brought the first revelation.
The first revelation came at the cave of Hira.
The first revelation came in Madinah.
easy.explain: The first revelation came at the cave of Hira, near Makkah, years before the migration to Madinah.

statements: Wudu can be invalidated and then repeated.
Ghusl is a full bath required in certain states.
Ghusl and wudu are exactly the same thing.
easy.explain: Wudu is the partial ablution before prayer; ghusl is the complete washing of the body required in specific states of impurity.

statements: Believing in the angels is an article of faith.
Believing in the Last Day is an article of faith.
Believing in the five pillars is one of the six articles of faith.
easy.explain: The five pillars are acts of Islam, not items in the list of six beliefs. The six articles are Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of the people of the cave.
Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of Dhul-Qarnayn.
Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of Yusuf.
medium.explain: The story of Yusuf is told in Surah Yusuf (12). Al-Kahf contains the cave sleepers, the two gardens, Musa and al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn.

statements: Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Luqman is surah 31.
Surah Yusuf is surah 10.
medium.explain: Surah Yusuf is surah 12. Surah 10 is Yunus.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was about forty when revelation began.
He lived about twenty-three years after that.
He lived about forty years after that.
medium.explain: Revelation lasted about twenty-three years, and the Prophet ﷺ was around sixty-three at his passing.

statements: Khadijah was the first to believe in the Prophet's message.
Khadijah died before the Hijrah.
Khadijah died after the conquest of Makkah.
medium.explain: Khadijah died around 619 CE in the Year of Sorrow, some three years before the Hijrah and eleven before the conquest of Makkah.

statements: Zakat is due once a lunar year has passed on qualifying wealth.
The nisab is the minimum threshold for zakat.
The nisab is the rate at which zakat is paid.
medium.explain: The nisab is the threshold of wealth; the rate on most savings is 2.5%.

statements: Surah Al-Ikhlas is about the oneness of Allah.
Surah Al-Kafirun addresses the disbelievers of Makkah.
Surah Al-Ikhlas is the longest surah in juz 30.
medium.explain: Al-Ikhlas has four ayahs and is among the shortest. The longest surah in juz 30 is An-Naba, with forty.

statements: The Ansar were from Madinah.
The Muhajirun emigrated from Makkah.
The Ansar emigrated from Makkah.
medium.explain: The Ansar were the helpers of Madinah who received the Muhajirun, the emigrants from Makkah.

statements: Tarawih is prayed in Ramadan.
Tahajjud is prayed after sleeping.
Tarawih is prayed before the Isha prayer.
medium.explain: Tarawih follows Isha. It is not prayed before it.

statements: The Qur'an has 30 ajza.
Juz 30 is called Juz Amma.
Juz 1 is called Juz Amma.
medium.explain: Juz Amma is the thirtieth, named after the opening words of Surah An-Naba, 'Amma yatasa'alun'.

statements: Sa'i is performed seven times between Safa and Marwah.
Tawaf is seven circuits of the Ka'bah.
Sa'i is performed three times.
medium.explain: Both Tawaf and Sa'i consist of seven, not three.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ had a daughter named Fatimah.
Fatimah married Ali ibn Abi Talib.
Fatimah married Uthman ibn Affan.
medium.explain: Fatimah married Ali ibn Abi Talib. Uthman married two of the Prophet's other daughters in succession, which is why he is called Dhun-Nurayn.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah contains Ayat al-Kursi.
Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255.
Ayat al-Kursi is a complete surah.
medium.explain: Ayat al-Kursi is a single verse within Surah Al-Baqarah, not a surah in its own right.

statements: The Hijri year has twelve months.
The Hijri calendar follows the moon.
The Hijri calendar follows the sun.
medium.explain: The Hijri calendar is lunar, which is why its months shift relative to the solar seasons.

statements: Umar ibn al-Khattab was the second caliph.
Umar accepted Islam in Makkah before the Hijrah.
Umar was the first caliph.
medium.explain: Abu Bakr was the first caliph; Umar succeeded him in 13 AH.

statements: Isa is called al-Masih in the Qur'an.
The Qur'an says Isa was raised up rather than killed.
The Qur'an says Isa was the son of Allah.
medium.explain: The Qur'an explicitly rejects this, affirming that Isa is a servant and messenger of Allah.

statements: The first qiblah was Jerusalem.
The qiblah changed to the Ka'bah.
The qiblah changed from the Ka'bah to Jerusalem.
medium.explain: The change ran the other way: from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah, during the Madinan period.

statements: Hajj has a fixed season.
Ihram is entered at a boundary called the miqat.
Ihram may be entered at any point, including inside Makkah, for Hajj from outside.
medium.explain: Those coming from outside enter ihram at the designated miqat before crossing into the sacred precinct.

statements: Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah.
They sheltered in the cave of Thawr.
They sheltered in the cave of Hira.
medium.explain: Hira is where the first revelation came, before the Hijrah. The cave on the migration journey was Thawr.

statements: A hadith has a chain of narrators and a text.
The chain is called the isnad.
The chain is called the matn.
medium.explain: The isnad is the chain of narrators; the matn is the text of the report.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is called Umm al-Kitab.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah.
Surah Al-Fatihah is the longest surah.
medium.explain: Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs. Al-Baqarah, with 286, is the longest.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf is surah 18.
Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Ta-Ha is surah 19.
hard.explain: Ta-Ha is surah 20, immediately after Maryam.

statements: Surah Al-Hajj contains a sajdah.
Surah As-Sajdah contains a sajdah.
Surah Al-Baqarah contains a sajdah.
hard.explain: Despite its length, Surah Al-Baqarah contains no verse of prostration.

statements: Khaybar was in 7 AH.
Hudaybiyyah was in 6 AH.
Hunayn was in 7 AH.
hard.explain: Hunayn was fought in 8 AH, shortly after the conquest of Makkah.

statements: Surah An-Naba has 40 ayahs.
Surah An-Nazi'at has 46 ayahs.
Surah Abasa has 60 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Abasa has 42 ayahs.

statements: Al-Nasa'i died in 915 CE.
Al-Tirmidhi died in 892 CE.
Al-Nasa'i died before al-Tirmidhi.
hard.explain: Al-Nasa'i outlived al-Tirmidhi by more than twenty years; he was the last of the six compilers to die.

statements: Surah Al-Imran has 200 ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'idah has 120 ayahs.
Surah Al-Anfal has 120 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anfal has 75 ayahs.

statements: The Battle of Siffin was fought during Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of the Camel was fought during Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of Siffin was fought during Uthman's caliphate.
hard.explain: Both Siffin and the Battle of the Camel took place during the caliphate of Ali, in the period of civil conflict known as the first fitnah.

statements: Surah Al-Fath was revealed in connection with Hudaybiyyah.
Surah Al-Anfal relates largely to Badr.
Surah Al-Hashr relates largely to Badr.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Hashr concerns the exile of Banu al-Nadir, not Badr.

statements: Surah Yunus is surah 10.
Surah Hud is surah 11.
Surah Ibrahim is surah 13.
hard.explain: Surah Ibrahim is surah 14. Surah 13 is Ar-Ra'd.

statements: Malik ibn Anas compiled the Muwatta.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal compiled a Musnad.
Al-Shafi'i compiled the Muwatta.
hard.explain: The Muwatta is Malik's. Al-Shafi'i, who studied under Malik, is known for al-Risalah and al-Umm.

statements: The Hijri calendar was formally instituted during Umar's caliphate.
Its first year corresponds to 622 CE.
It was formally instituted during Abu Bakr's caliphate.
hard.explain: The calendar was formally established under Umar, who set its starting point at the year of the Hijrah.

statements: Surah Al-Waqi'ah is surah 56.
Surah Al-Hadid is surah 57.
Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 56.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55, immediately before Al-Waqi'ah.

statements: Zayd ibn Thabit led the compilation under Abu Bakr.
He was also central to the standardisation under Uthman.
He was a Muhajir from Makkah.
hard.explain: Zayd ibn Thabit was from Madinah and so was among the Ansar, not the Muhajirun.

statements: Surah Al-Mulk has 30 ayahs.
Surah Nuh has 28 ayahs.
Surah Al-Jinn has 18 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Jinn has 28 ayahs. Surah Al-Jinn and Surah Nuh both have 28.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant by the traditional account.
He was about forty at the first revelation.
He was about thirty at the first revelation.
hard.explain: The traditional account places the first revelation at about the age of forty.

statements: Surah Al-Ankabut is surah 29.
Surah Ar-Rum is surah 30.
Surah As-Sajdah is surah 31.
hard.explain: As-Sajdah is surah 32. Surah 31 is Luqman.

statements: Abu Hanifah is associated with Kufa.
Malik ibn Anas is associated with Madinah.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal is associated with Madinah.
hard.explain: Ahmad ibn Hanbal is associated with Baghdad. Malik is the one associated with Madinah.

statements: Surah Al-Qadr describes a night better than a thousand months.
Surah Al-Qadr has five ayahs.
Surah Al-Qadr is a Madinan surah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qadr (97) is generally classified as Makkan, though a minority view holds otherwise.

statements: Tabuk took place in 9 AH.
The Farewell Pilgrimage took place in 10 AH.
The Farewell Pilgrimage took place in 9 AH.
hard.explain: The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 10 AH, the year before the Prophet's passing in 11 AH.

statements: Surah Al-Fil has five ayahs.
Surah Quraysh has four ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'un has four ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'un has seven ayahs.
